comment: I had him a really long time ago. He was a nice guy and he seemed to care about his students, but he made biology, which was by far my favorite subject, mind-numbingly boring.

Dr. Radice, although a really nice guy, failed  to meet expectations.  He didnt really teach us anything, he just droned in front of the class and somehow still expected us to know information for the tests.  Hes retiring now so this review wont mean anything but I at least want it to go down in history as the worst bio class I have ever taken.

Radice is very hard to understand and all his presentations come directly from the book. It's hard to gain a new perspective on the subject when he uses the same information found in the textbook. His tests are not similar to his notes at all and are very hard to follow. If you can avoid taking his class, then you will be straight.
Really unclear during lecture; very inconsistent when writings tests.  Cannot answer his own questions.  Lecture is a sleeper.

Dr. Radice is hard, but since when has college been about taking slacker classes? He is fair, funny and most importantly makes you think. His tests can be difficult if you don't study-so study! His lectures can get detailed and a bit boring at 8AM, but he obviously cares about what he does. Overall a good professor!
Does not know how to teach at all. Slideshows are figures from the textbook, lectures are pointless and do not relate to the exams.

He was extremely helpful, however it didn't help with the poor quality of lecture. His lectures were very unclear and he is very unclear about what you should know for the tests. He does alot of hypothesis thinking in his class without helping you find the answers. Not an easy or clear professor for this subject.
he is really nice but his class is hard and stuff but he takes the time out to listen to what you have to say

Obviously the people who rated Dr. Radice weren't science majors, or went to some easy school where it was easy to get such a good GPA. Dr. Radice is an awesome professor and he really knows what he is talking about.  He is one of the best biology teachers I've had at Richmond and he is a really great guy.  Definately someone to take.
how did radice get a chile?  this class should not be a 100 level.  it is too challenging for a gen ed.
Hard for a non-bio major, but study guides are very useful. He's accomodating and wants to see his students succeed.

i had this guy years back before i really got into biology. his tests and quizzes were always very difficult, it never seemed like i could have studied anymore than i did. i got a C in his class, transferred to another legit school and graduated with a 3.9 gpa in bio...

Just make sure you do all of the study guides for the exams and do decently on the quizzes which he pretty much tells you the questions to, and you'll do fine.  Attendance is optional but its a good idea to go to most of the classes if you don't read the book.
